clesRetenues: Q Travis Steed (BofA) - part ACA vs maturation naturelle dans le ralentissement US : le management confirme une combinaison des deux effets (12% T2 vs 14% T1), sans isoler la part exacte de chacun.

Q Travis Steed (BofA) - retour des procedures differees au S2 : pas de reponse chiffree directe ; le management renvoie a la dynamique EUP 2027, decrite comme un impact PROGRESSIF sur 2027 (pas un effet de seuil), par analogie au cycle EUP 2020 deja assimile en interne.

Q Rick Wise (Stifel) - rationale et TAM du nouveau robot flexible GI : le management ne chiffre pas le TAM incremental a ce stade, evoque une serie de mises a jour "standout" prevues sur plusieurs annees a venir.

Q Lawrence Biggleson (Wells Fargo) - la robotique sera-t-elle incluse dans le nouveau programme VBP centralise chinois : le management confirme explicitement que "nous pensons que la robotique en fera partie", phase-in attendu sur les prochains trimestres, sans detail supplementaire.

Q Lawrence Biggleson (Wells Fargo) - benefice tangible du nouveau chiffrement des instruments : positionne comme un renforcement de la securite/qualite/disponibilite des produits, en reponse a la pression concurrentielle des instruments reconditionnes tiers.

Q Ryan Zimmerman (BTIG) - impact de la prudence clients sur l'ACA vs pipeline capex : le management confirme un signal de prudence de la part de certains clients sur les inscriptions ACA, mais precise que cela n'a PAS affecte le pipeline capital a ce jour.

Q Vic Koptra (BMO) - ampleur potentielle de la contribution du Japon post-remboursement : TAM non chiffre, le management identifie la hernie inguinale comme la plus grosse procedure couverte par le nouveau remboursement, promet une mise a jour ulterieure.

Q Michael Pollack (Wolf Research) - dynamique de mix/prix sur l'INA par procedure : le management confirme un effet de mix positif (produits a innovation incrementale, pricing plus eleve) partiellement compense par d'autres dynamiques, quantification differee au prochain call.

Q Vijay Kumar (Evercore) - exposition precise Medicaid/echanges ACA : le management n'a PAS d'estimation precise ; la majorite du CA vient de l'assurance privee/commerciale, Medicare et Medicaid representent des parts plus faibles.

Q Vijay Kumar (Evercore) - comparables T3 plus difficiles : confirme par le CFO, avec un double effet - comp US plus dur (deja note l'an dernier) ET un decalage calendaire international qui avait deplace de la croissance du T4 2025 vers le T3 2025, effet non repete a l'identique en 2026.

epsReported.note: GAAP diluted EPS $2.29 vs $1.81 a year ago (+27%); GAAP net income $818M. Cross-checked vs stockanalysis.com quarterly financials.

dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: No formal quarterly guidance (as usual), but management flagged two Q3 headwinds: a tougher US comp flagged a year ago, and international seasonal holiday shifts that moved volume from Q4 to Q3 last year (affecting Q3 and Q4 comparisons); H1 ran close to 15% da Vinci procedure growth, with H2 guided toward the midpoint of the annual range.
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: FY26 da Vinci procedure growth maintained at 13.5%-15.5% but now expected closer to the midpoint (range factors: ACA subsidy expiry and US patient behavior, China tender volumes and competitive intensity, European budget pressure, Japan capital constraints, GLP-1 impact on bariatrics); non-GAAP gross margin RAISED to 68%-69% (from 67.5%-68.5%), including the one-off $36M IEEPA tariff refund (~68.7% underlying in Q2) and despite freight and semiconductor memory cost inflation; non-GAAP opex growth trimmed to 11%-13% with R&D deliberately growing faster than SG&A; SBC $880-900M; other income $315-335M; non-GAAP tax rate 22%-23%.
pointsCles: US da Vinci procedure growth decelerated to 12% (vs 14% in Q1), concentrated in deferrable benign procedures; management attributes it to expiring enhanced ACA premium subsidies plus law of large numbers, says underlying disease burden is unchanged and deferred cases will return; bariatric still down high single digits on GLP-1s; no impact seen on the capital pipeline so far.

Strong capital quarter: 468 da Vinci placements (+18%), of which 246 da Vinci 5 (114 dual consoles) and 38 SP, plus 55 Ion; US placements +24% but roughly half were trade-ins (upgrades to dV5, 144 trade-ins vs 83), so net US installed-base expansion is moderating and system utilization (+3% da Vinci, +11% Ion, +25% SP US) becomes the key metric; dV5 base now >1,700 systems, first My Intuitive+ renewals saw zero opt-outs.

Extended Use Program confirmed for H1 2027 on a subset of Gen 4/Gen 5 EndoWrist instruments (Force Feedback, stapling and energy excluded): deliberate cut in customer cost per use targeting high-volume benign procedures, ASCs and cost-constrained geographies; impact on I&A per procedure (~$1,830 in Q2) not yet quantified, framed as progressive through 2027 like the 2020 program.

Geographic mix diverging: OUS da Vinci procedures +20% with India (dV5 clearance obtained), Italy, Taiwan, UK strong and OUS benign procedures accelerating to +37%; Japan turning up on June 1 reimbursement additions (25 placements vs 15); China still hard (2 placements, weak tenders, domestic competition, price pressure) with tender centralization that management explicitly does NOT equate to VBP; new pipeline options include a non-commercial GI flexible robotic endoscope filed for 510(k) and instrument encryption reinforcing the consumables moat.

hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Undisputed leader in robot-assisted surgery (da Vinci, Ion, SP): installed base >13,000 systems (+12% YoY) and ~85% recurring revenue (instruments/accessories/service). The thesis: surgical-robotics penetration compounds for a decade, powered by a still-early da Vinci 5 replacement cycle and international expansion. FY26 guided: procedures +13.5/15.5%, non-GAAP gross margin RAISED to 68-69% at Q2. The 07/08 refresh arbitrated the 2026 EPS DOWN from a naive seasonal extrapolation (~9.50) to 9.24: the 2025 H2/H1 ratio was contaminated by a calendar shift and management explicitly signaled deceleration.

== THESIS READ ==
- Procedure growth is the leading indicator and it held its band through H1. Watch: Q3 procedure print and any bariatric/international mix commentary.
- The EPS arbitration (E5 ter): quarterly build confronted with the annual figure exposed the seasonal-ratio trap - the model deliberately sits below naive extrapolation. Watch: Q3 (20/10, confirmed) validates or invalidates the deceleration read.
- da Vinci 5 rollout is still supply-gated with a rich upgrade backlog. Watch: dV5 placement mix and pricing capture.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Consensus non-GAAP (10.41) vs Omnium base keeping SBC/amortization (9.24) - definitional wedge documented. Net cash ~9.5bn growing to ~13bn; interest income explicit in the bridge; ETR 20% normative (FY25 actual ~17% on excess SBC benefits, documented). Guides procedures/margin, never EPS.

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
2026: revenue 12.1bn (+20%), EBIT 3.75bn (31%), EPS 9.24 (arbitrated); 2027-2030: revenue +15%/yr fading, margin drift to 33.5%, shares -0.5%/yr. Watch: Q3 print (20/10); dV5 international regulatory clearances; competitive entries (Hugo, Ottava) in procedure share data.

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 (20/10); dV5 ex-US approvals; new procedure clearances (Ion expansion); FY27 procedure guidance (Jan).

ancrages.moteur: Croissance procedures da Vinci+Ion guidee a 13,5-15,5% pour 2026 (visee au point median ~14,5%), ralentissant graduellement vers ~10% en 2030 sous l'effet de la loi des grands nombres sur la base installee.

La croissance du CA depasse la croissance procedurale grace au mix da Vinci 5/SP et a l'ASP par procedure ; prime de ~4pts en 2026, s'attenuant vers ~2pts d'ici 2030 avec la maturation de la penetration da Vinci 5.
Marge brute non-GAAP 2026 relevee a 68-69% ; expansion GAAP graduelle de ~100-150 pb/an jusqu'en 2028 puis plateau.
Croissance opex non-GAAP guidee 11-13% pour 2026 (R&D > SG&A) ; decelaration graduelle vers le rythme de croissance du CA d'ici 2028-2029.
Taux d'impot GAAP normalise a 18%, entre le taux historique recent anormalement bas (effet windfall SBC) et le taux non-GAAP guide (22-23%) qui exclut structurellement ce meme windfall.

Extended Use Program (S1 2027) reduit intentionnellement le prix par procedure sur un sous-ensemble d'instruments ; impact toujours non quantifie par le management (confirme T2 26, deploiement decrit comme progressif), haircut prudent de ~1-1,5pt maintenu sur la prime de mix/ASP 2027-2028.

Position nette de tresorerie croissante (zero dette financiere, ~9,0 Md$ fin 2025) genere des autres revenus croissants (guides 315-335 M$ pour 2026), continue de s'accroitre malgre les rachats d'actions.

Arbitrage T2 26 (E5 ter point 4) : omniumEPS 2026 rebase de 9,06 a 9,24 (+2,0%) sur la base d'une prime saisonniere H2/H1 damped a +5,75% (moitie du ratio brut 2025, juge contamine par un decalage calendaire ponctuel et le signal de decelaration explicite du management) ; toute la trajectoire 2027-2030 rebasee proportionnellement, marges/ratios inchanges.
